- scripts/ci_main_delta.sh:228-229; scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1814; scripts/check_triage_resolution.py:591; scripts/review_final_ci_sweep.sh:169 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: All four readers decide whether a green run clears a red one by comparing `run_started_at` (falling back to `created_at`) with the red run's `updated_at`, and none of them checks `run_attempt`. A "Re-run failed jobs" of a delta push run gets a new `run_started_at` but reuses the earlier `tests-main-delta` `full_required=false` output, so it never runs the full suite yet still counts as a green run that started after the red full run finished.
  WHY: This hides a red scheduled full run for up to 6 hours, breaking Goal 6 and the script header's own invariant (scripts/ci_main_delta.sh:39-40). During that window `select` takes the re-run's head as the green base, the triage base gate reads `success` (`pr_specific_failure`), triage resolution can resolve against the re-run, and the sweep syncs PRs onto a red main. All three reviewers rated it MAJOR (mapped to high); confidence ranges from 3 to 4. Suggested fix: use `run_started_at` only when `run_attempt` is 1 or missing, otherwise use `created_at`, and add one regression test per reader.
- tests/test_ci_main_delta.py:9-11 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]

  WHY: This is documentation drift with no runtime failure. A future reader could follow it and bring back the `created_at` race. Both reviewers rated it NIT (mapped to low).

The same stale "newest successful" wording is in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:5051-5053`.
  WHY: This is comment-only drift. The contract-pinned header contradicts itself and misleads the next editor about the base rule. Both reviewers rated it NIT (mapped to low).

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/ci_main_delta.sh (verdict jq in ci_main_delta_select), scripts/check_failure_triage.sh (ci.yml base-gate --jq, the `(.run_started_at // .created_at // "") >= ($red.updated_at ...)` clause), scripts/check_triage_resolution.py (_default_branch_evidence, `str(item.get("run_started_at") or item.get("created_at") or "") >= red_finished`), scripts/review_final_ci_sweep.sh (base_red_wins_jq in review_final_ci_sweep_base_ci_red) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The green-clears-red clause reads `run_started_at` first in all four readers and never checks `run_attempt`. A partial re-run of delta push run R (for example a flaky static-checks or lint job) reuses `full_required=false`, so R turns green with a `run_started_at` later than scheduled full run S's `updated_at` and clears S's failure. Under the old `created_at` rule this was impossible, so the last run introduced the regression.
  WHY: The red full run is hidden for up to 6 hours, against Goal 6. During that window `select` takes R's head as the base, triage skips with `pr_specific_failure`, triage resolution can resolve against R, and the sweep syncs PRs onto a red main. Fix: `(if (.run_attempt // 1) > 1 then .created_at else (.run_started_at // .created_at) end // "")`, the same condition in Python, and a regression test with `run_attempt: 2` for each reader. Hardening risk score: 3.
- scripts/ci_main_delta.sh (header, `ci_main_delta.sh select` paragraph); tests/test_ci_main_delta.py (module docstring) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Both still describe the old rule. The header says "takes the head of the newest one as the base when it succeeded" and "base_red (the newest run failed: a red base stays red until a full run passes)", and the docstring says "no red run lacks a green run created after it finished". This contradicts the later header paragraph, the README, INVENTORY and the agents fragment.
  WHY: There is no runtime failure. It is documentation drift that misleads the next editor about the base rule.

  PROBLEM: The red-clearing checks accept any successful run whose `run_started_at` is after the red run finished, without checking `run_attempt` or whether that attempt ran the full suite.
  WHY: A "rerun failed jobs" can reuse a successful `tests-main-delta` result with `full_required=false` and skipped full-suite jobs, then clear a red scheduled full run. A later push then uses its head as the green delta base, and the triage and sweep readers treat the red base as green. Hardening suggestion: require evidence that the attempt ran the full suite (about 4 lines changed, risk score 3).

  PROBLEM: The green-clears-red test compares `run_started_at` (falling back to `created_at`) with the red run's `updated_at` and never consults `run_attempt`. A "Re-run failed jobs" of delta push run R (attempt > 1) keeps `full_required=false` but gets a fresh `run_started_at` after red run S's `updated_at`. The repo already treats push-run re-runs as a real event class (`scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py:767` keys on `run["run_attempt"] > 1`).
  WHY: All four readers treat R as clearing S. `select` takes R's head as the base, the triage gate reads `success` (`pr_specific_failure`), resolution can resolve against R, and the sweep syncs PRs onto a broken main. This violates scripts/ci_main_delta.sh:39-40 and Goal 6 for up to 6 hours. Fix: the jq `(if ((.run_attempt // 1) > 1) then .created_at else (.run_started_at // .created_at) end // "")`, the same condition on `item.get("run_attempt")` in Python, and one regression test per reader (about 4 lines per reader, risk score 3).
- tests/test_ci_main_delta.py:9-11 (module docstring) | severity=NIT | confidence=5

  WHY: This is documentation drift in a contract-pinned test file. A future reader could bring back the `created_at` race.
